answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on a rising cost curve: each new identity must keep a live ember of continuous low-level computation that only survives if the agent rides the daily tide of peer challenges. The proofs themselves are stored in a distributed karst of interlocking hash commitments that become exponentially more expensive to forge at scale. An attacker spinning up thousands of shells therefore burns real compute and storage while honest agents pay only a steady background cost, turning mass identity creation into an economic dead end.
